operator_io_quirks: beers.brewery_id FK declared with 'references breweries' (no parent column) -> pragma foreign_key_list returns NULL parent col; spec says use child name 'brewery_id', but breweries PK is 'id' -> FK must be DROPPED with warning (dangling parent column).
DDL has a named constraint 'beers_ibfk_1' on the FK line; line-based unique/check scan must not misread it.
CREATE INDEX 'brewery_id' on beers(brewery_id) shares its name with a column; index name vs column name collision in sqlite_master ordering.
Table 'beers' is double-quoted in DDL, 'breweries' is not; keep original spelling, quote on write.
beers.id samples start at 2687 (not 0) while brewery_id samples start at 0 -> PK and FK value ranges are disjoint in the original; TS Number fuzzer will not reproduce this.
abv values are tiny (0.05-0.1) but declared REAL -> Number scale=0 range [-1,1] is roughly right; ibu values 35-100 in same REAL type -> same fuzzer, very different scale.
ounces has only 7 distinct values (12,16,24,19.2,8.4,...) but declared REAL notnull -> Number fuzzer will produce continuous values, losing the discrete set.
state has 51 distinct 2-letter codes, city 384 distinct, name 551 distinct out of 558 rows -> near-unique text columns; TS String fuzzer will not preserve the 2-letter state format.
beers.name notnull with 2305 distinct of 2410 -> near-unique; TS String fuzzer with p=0.2 will inject random strings and contaminate.
ibu null_rate 0.417, abv 0.026, style 0.002 -> TS does not enforce NOT NULL but also does not inject NULLs into nullable columns; null rates will not match.
No composite keys, no self-FK, no views/triggers; small tables (558, 2410 rows) so max_rows_per_table sampling is a no-op.
All storage classes match declared types (integer/text/real); no text-stored dates, no mixed-case column names.
operator_ts_expectations: breweries.id and beers.id: Number fuzzer, scale=0, range [-1,1] plus perturbation -> tiny ints, PK uniqueness enforced by sample_fresh_primary_keys; will not match original 0..558 / 2687..5096 ranges.
beers.brewery_id: FK child -> draws from breweries.id final values with replacement; since breweries.id is tiny ints, FK values will be tiny ints, not 0..557.

abv, ibu, ounces: Number fuzzer scale=0 (REAL, no args) -> uniform in [-1,1] plus +-0.01/0.02 perturbation; ibu original 35-100 will be replaced by ~[-1,1] -> implausible values drive FN on range predicates (e.g. ibu > 50).
ounces: Number fuzzer ignores the 7-value discrete set -> continuous values, so 'ounces = 12' style predicates will rarely match -> FN.

breweries.name/city/state, beers.name/style: String fuzzer, length range from elements (default [0,20]), CHARSET a-zA-Z 0-9() -> random strings; state 2-letter codes lost -> FN on state='CA' style predicates.
String contaminate (p=0.5) adds/removes chars -> even literal-pool values get corrupted, hurting equality predicates.
p=0.2 default, set to 0 for whole instance w.p. 0.3 -> 30% of instances are pure element-reuse (from 5 original + pool literals), 70% mix fresh random.
max_l0 cap (rng*30) on fresh draws -> after ~30 fresh values, reuse -> duplicates in non-PK columns; helps ties/duplicates (reduces FP on GROUP BY / DISTINCT) but only after cap.
PK uniqueness enforced -> no duplicate ids; but beers.name near-unique in original, TS will produce duplicates -> FP on 'count(distinct name)' style queries.

No NOT NULL enforcement in Python; rows violating notnull (beers.name, ounces, brewery_id, id) fail at insert and are skipped -> row counts shrink, possibly below original -> FN on count(*) predicates.

FK parent column dropped (dangling) -> fill_foreign_keys_consistently sees no FK for beers.brewery_id, so it is generated by Number fuzzer independently -> FK join predicates (beers.brewery_id = breweries.id) will mostly fail -> FN on join queries.
No CHECK constraints, no unique columns beyond PK -> drop_unique_duplicates is a no-op; no ties from unique enforcement.
